name: Robert Altman

summary.text: Robert A. Altman (1947-2021) was a Washington lawyer and law partner of Clark Clifford who became president of First American Bankshares after the 1981-82 takeover of Financial General Bankshares by investors the Federal Reserve later found were fronting for BCCI; he and Clifford also acted as counsel to BCCI. He was indicted by federal and New York grand juries in July 1992; the court dismissed the central bribery count for lack of evidence and a Manhattan jury acquitted him on August 14, 1993, after which the federal indictment was dismissed. In February 1998 he and Clifford settled the Federal Reserve's administrative proceedings without admitting the allegations, transferring holding-company shares valued at about $5 million. He later ran the video-game company ZeniMax Media and died on February 3, 2021. The BCCI, Clark Clifford and First American files hold the Senate findings; this file holds what is specific to Altman.

facts.claim: After a group of foreign investors the Federal Reserve later found were fronting for BCCI took control of First American Bankshares, Altman, then in his early thirties, was named First American's president and Clark Clifford its chairman; both men also acted as counsel to BCCI.
facts.quote: Altman, then in his early 30s, was named First American's president. Clifford became chairman, and both men also acted as counsel to BCCI.

facts.claim: The Senate Foreign Relations Committee's December 1992 report on BCCI devotes a chapter to Clifford and Altman, finding that beginning in late 1977 they assisted BCCI in purchasing Financial General Bankshares with the participation of nominees while understanding BCCI's central involvement in directing and controlling the transaction, and that both men participated in some of BCCI's deceptions in the United States.
facts.quote: BCCI - CLARK CLIFFORD AND ROBERT ALTMAN

facts.claim: Altman was indicted in July 1992 together with his law partner Clark Clifford, who was found too ill to stand trial. On August 14, 1993, after the court dismissed the central bribery count because the government had presented no evidence to support it, a Manhattan jury acquitted Altman of all remaining charges that he deceived banking regulators in the BCCI case, and the Justice Department then dismissed the companion federal indictment.
facts.quote: Altman was acquitted late on Aug. 14, 1993 by a jury of eight women and four men of all charges that he deceived banking regulators in the BCCI case.

sources.title: Altman acquitted in massive BCCI fraud trial

facts.claim: On February 3, 1998, the Federal Reserve Board announced it had settled, with their consent, its administrative proceedings against Clifford and Altman; without admitting the Board's allegations the two agreed to pay approximately $5 million in compensation by transferring their interest in most of their shares of the holding company for the benefit of BCCI's depositors and creditors.
facts.quote: Without admitting the Board's allegations, the two agreed to pay approximately $5 million in compensation by transferring their interest in most of their shares of the holding company.

sources.title: Settlement of administrative proceedings against Clark M. Clifford and Robert A. Altman

facts.claim: The Senate BCCI report records that in October 1991 Altman, as former president of First American, told the Subcommittee that the CIA had made extensive use of First American for a variety of purposes including ordinary banking and savings accounts, which Acting CIA Director Richard Kerr acknowledged the next day.
facts.quote: the CIA had made extensive use of First American

sources.publisher: U.S. Senate Committee on Foreign Relations (via FAS)

facts.claim: After the BCCI case Altman became chief executive of ZeniMax Media, the video-game company behind Bethesda Softworks, which he built into a multibillion-dollar business; he died on February 3, 2021 in Baltimore at age 73.
facts.quote: Altman went on to become chief executive of ZeniMax Media, a video game company he built into a multibillion-dollar business.

connections.claim: Altman was president of First American Bankshares from the 1982 takeover until 1991, and the Federal Reserve stated in 1998 that he and Clifford had served as directors of Credit and Commerce American Holdings and of its subsidiary First American Bankshares.
